observations: The globe is visible with continuous textured limbs in both lighting states and the recorded drag endpoints; no broad missing faces or former dark dotted loops were observed.

Elevation shows a full ≤−1 / 0 / ≥1 km scale, its ellipsoid datum, clipping and gray missing-data grid. The corrected JPL v2 shape is distinguished from the earlier Schenk elevation product; invalid original v1 is excluded visibly.
Neutral shape grid is continuous. Minor grid aliasing at DPR1 limbs and faceted terminator shading remain; this is not pixel-perfect rendering qualification.

The controlled mosaic and enhanced Cassini infrared/green/ultraviolet image have continuous limbs and matching broad features at both DPRs and drag endpoints. Uneven source detail, image shadows and source seams are visible and explicitly qualified.

Elevation has a complete −12.5 / 0 / +12.5 km scale, a 531 km reference sphere, fixed northwest relief and separate approximate globe lighting. The ~1.5 km posted height grid is distinguished from simplified Q128 geometry.

Relative albedo is visibly a subtle pale field. Copy distinguishes the normalized secondary model from visible color/calibrated reflectance, states lower validation and saturated 0.5–1.5 display with gray gaps.

No exposed interior or former dotted contour in the neutral shape grid. Broad triangular lighting transitions and faint thin face edges remain in some lit views. Earlier relative-albedo right legend label is ellipsized; this historical finding is resolved by the 12-image corrected-card supplement.
Final corrected relative-albedo and elevation cards were visually inspected at both DPRs: complete units, no ellipsis/overlap, and full scientific description visible.

Normal and enhanced composites remain continuous at the inspected limb and drag endpoints. Enhanced copy states infrared/green/ultraviolet, enhanced colors, and retained shadows/seams; the visible pale tones and varying detail are consistent with that bounded meaning.
Elevation has a complete −7.5 / 0 / +7.5 km scale and 561.4 km reference sphere; ~1.58 km grid spacing and separate simplified Q128 geometry are visible.

Relative albedo is visibly separate and correctly qualified as a normalized, less-validated secondary model rather than measured calibrated reflectance. Earlier right legend label is ellipsized; this historical finding is resolved by the 12-image corrected-card supplement.

The shape grid is closed in the inspected views. Faint angular edges near the lit elevation terminator and broader faceted lighting in lit relative albedo remain, with no broad missing patches or exposed interior.
Final corrected relative-albedo and elevation cards were visually inspected at both DPRs: complete units, no ellipsis/overlap, and full scientific description visible.
Former central dark dotted loops are absent from the inspected shape and surface views at both DPRs, including the lit drag endpoint. Limbs remain continuous.

Elevation shows the complete −10 / 0 / +10 km scale, 763.5 km reference sphere and ~2.15 km posting. Revised text explicitly describes the producer's simulation-based one-to-two-grid-spacing estimate and says it is not an independent Rhea uncertainty measurement.

Relative albedo shows subtle brightness variation and the required model/calibration/coverage limits. Earlier right legend label is ellipsized; this historical finding is resolved by the 12-image corrected-card supplement.

Enhanced color displays the olive/gray hemisphere contrast and source seams visible in the preview, while copy explicitly qualifies hemisphere differences, shadows and seams. Both lighting states and drag endpoints remain coherent.
Minor DPR1 limb grid aliasing and broad faceted lighting/very fine triangle edges remain in some lit pale views. No broad surface hole observed.
Final corrected relative-albedo and elevation cards were visually inspected at both DPRs: complete units, no ellipsis/overlap, and full scientific description visible.
Near-infrared imagery is continuous in the inspected views and explicitly retains clouds, seams and uneven detail.

Measured height appears as sparse colored tracks over gray unavailable cells. Full −2500 / 0 / +2500 m legend, 2575.0 km reference sphere, ~6.0% coverage, 0.125° posting/~5.62 km equatorial spacing, variable footprints and no shape deformation are visible.

Interpolated height is a filled model field, clearly described as estimates between the sparse inputs; distance to data is separately colored and described as nearest input distance, not height uncertainty or all-instrument coverage. Full distance scale is 0 / 500 / 1000 km.

Faint dotted triangular boundaries remain in DPR1 pale overlays, especially unlit interpolated height, with weaker traces in distance-to-data. They are much less visible at DPR2. No broad missing patch or torn limb observed; do not interpret those traces as terrain.
Radar is outside this captured/reviewed lens selection.
Replacement capture shows continuous mosaic, enhanced-color and elevation views at both DPRs and recorded lit drag endpoints. Gray unavailable southern/color/height coverage remains explicit.

Enhanced-color visible copy now explicitly identifies MVIC near-infrared/red/blue, panchromatic sharpening, enhanced appearance, non-natural color and non-quantitative-albedo meaning; unavailable color and variable detail are visible limits.
Elevation is connected to the complete −15 / 0 / 15 km scale and describes stereo/shading height relative to a 606 km sphere, variable detail and gray missing cells.
Fine angular boundaries are visible near the enhanced-color DPR1 limb, less visible at DPR2. No broad hole or new blocker observed.

limitations: Original integrated report is globally INVALID due to Charon navigation ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. Completed five Saturn body cases are individually usable; the failed Charon case is replaced by the separate completed Charon report. This review does not relabel the original report as passing.
1440x1000 CSS viewport only. Original DPR2 PNGs are 2880x2000; view_image displayed resized 1889x1312 previews, so fine pixel-level conclusions are bounded.

Default recorded poses and one lit drag endpoint only. Not a full rotation, all-pole, close-up, high-zoom, mobile, performance, source/native-pixel-parity or current-live-state qualification. Dark hemispheres do not expose all surface microdetail.
Capture HEAD values and exact frozenFiles must both be retained because shell/card fixes may have been dirty at capture.
No observed broad holes does not prove an absence of every subpixel seam. Remaining faceting and faint DPR1 triangle boundaries are documented as presentation limits, not measured terrain.
